newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks surge, end at third straight record.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks surge, end at third straight record.

text.p: Caracas stocks surged in strong trade to close at a third straight record high as bullish sentiment continued to spill over from a ground-breaking labor reform bill signed Thursday, traders said.
"We continue to see both local and foreign investors buying stocks, taking positions," Union broker Hector Perez said.
The bill paves the way for a revamping of Venezuela's decaying social security system. By capping workers' severance pay, ministers say the law will also boost jobs and wages.
The bolsa's 19-share .IBC roared ahead 2.1 percent, busting through resistance to close at 8,008.93 points.
Market bellwether Electricidad de Caracas led gainers, rising 3.23 percent to end at 608.00 bolivars.
"The market really took note of that rise. To break through 600 bolivars is an important barrier," Perez said.
Among traded issues, 34 rose, eight fell, and two closed flat as a total of 145 million shares changed hands, worth 11.8 billion bolivars ($24 million).
The Merinvest composite .MRCP index, which includes telephone company CANTV, meanwhile closed ahead 1.74 percent to end at 123.85 percent.
